why: There is no single posture that is correct for every person or task. Comfort, time in one position, workload, movement options, and the individual all matter.

slides.title: Posture & Pain
slides.content: Posture can affect comfort and load, but one position does not explain persistent pain by itself.

slides.title: The Real Story
slides.content: Bodies naturally use many positions. A posture that feels comfortable for one person or task may not suit another.

slides.title: Movement Matters
slides.content: Instead of policing every position, build options: change positions when useful, move regularly, and develop capacity for the demands that matter to you.

slides.title: Time and Context Matter
slides.content: The same posture may feel fine briefly and uncomfortable when sustained. Task duration, fatigue, stress, sensitivity, and available support can change the experience.

slides.title: Myth vs Fact
slides.content: Myth: There is one safe posture everyone should hold. Better question: Which positions are comfortable and useful for this person, task, and duration?

slides.title: Try this today
slides.content: During one repeated task, try two or three comfortable positions and brief movement breaks. Notice which options help rather than searching for perfect alignment.

title: Posture is an option, not a verdict
